content: Engulfment and cell motility protein 1 (ELMO1) is a protein encoded by the ELMO1 gene in humans. The ELMO1 gene is located on chromosome 7 in humans and on chromosome 13 in mice. Structure The ELMO1 protein in humans is composed of 720 amino acid residues. It contains three distinct domains: 1. N-terminal Armadillo domain: This domain spans residues 82 to 262. 2. Central ELMO domain: This domain is located between residues 301 and 492. 3. C-terminal pleckstrin homology (PH) domain: This domain spans residues 527 to 674. Additionally, ELMO1 has a proline-rich motif at its extreme C-terminus. Secondary structure predictions indicate the presence of alpha-helical regions at both the N-terminus and C-terminus of the protein. The three-dimensional structure of the pleckstrin homology domain has been resolved using X-ray crystallography. Function The ELMO1 protein interacts with the dedicator of cytokinesis 1 (DOCK1) protein to facilitate phagocytosis and mediate changes in cell shape. Based on its similarity to a protein in Caenorhabditis elegans, ELMO1 is thought to play a role in apoptosis and cell migration. The ELMO1 gene undergoes alternative splicing, resulting in multiple transcript variants that encode different isoforms of the protein. Interactions ELMO1 has been shown to interact with several proteins, including DOCK180 and hematopoietic cell kinase (HCK). The interaction between ELMO1 and the SH3 domain of HCK is mediated by polyproline interactions. When ELMO1 forms a complex with DOCK180, it activates Rac GTPase-dependent biological processes. The pleckstrin homology domain of ELMO1 plays a critical role in stabilizing DOCK180 and protecting it from degradation. Binding of ELMO1 to DOCK180 alleviates steric inhibition of DOCK180, thereby enabling the activation of Rac GTPase. The proline-rich motif at the C-terminus of ELMO1 is essential for its binding to the SH3 domain at the N-terminus of DOCK180. The ELMO1-DOCK180 complex serves as a key regulator of Rac GTPase activity during cell development and migration. Mutations that disrupt the interaction sites between ELMO1 and DOCK180 result in the destabilization of the ELMO1-DOCK180 complex. Furthermore, when ELMO1 forms a complex with both DOCK180 and CrkII, it achieves maximal efficiency in promoting phagocytosis. This molecular complex functions upstream of Rac GTPase during the process of phagocytosis.
